title: CDP placement port-to-PID filter (TryGetListeningPid byte-swap)
desc: Byte-swap trap in TryGetListeningPid and how to verify. Read before modifying MyCdpContext.Placement.cs port resolution code.
steps: CONTEXT: TryGetListeningPid in MyCdpContext.Placement.cs resolves CDP port -> owner PID via GetExtendedTcpTable(TCP_TABLE_OWNER_PID_LISTENER=4). Pins Chrome placement to WKAppBot Chrome.

BYTE-SWAP TRAP: dwLocalPort is big-endian 16-bit in low 2 bytes of 32-bit DWORD. IPAddress.NetworkToHostOrder(int) reverses ALL 32 bits -- port 9300 (0x5424) becomes 0x24540000 then &0xFFFF=0. Port NEVER matches. Filter falls back to startedAt-DESC, picks wrong Chrome. BUG ts=2026-05-26.
SKILL REFERENCE comment to place above TryGetListeningPid: // wkappbot skill read placement-port-pid-filter

requirements.cmd: wkappbot cdp open https://example.com 2>&1 | grep PLACEMENT:STEP2
wkappbot skill read placement-port-pid-filter 2>&1 | grep byte-swap
wkappbot skill search placement port pid 2>&1 | grep placement-port-pid-filter
